triples.relationship: A spiritual quality represented as a shield
triples.rationale: Wisdom depicts God taking holiness as an invincible shield within His armor. Ephesians instructs the hearers to take faith as a shield that extinguishes flaming arrows. Both give a spiritual quality the defensive role of a shield, while the bearer and the named quality differ; holiness is not silently changed into faith.
triples.source_text: He will take holiness as an invincible shield,

target_units.text: in all circumstances taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.

triples.relationship: A feared leader who nevertheless wins the people's regard
triples.rationale: Wisdom expects rulers to fear the wise speaker while the multitude regards him well. Saul fears David and becomes wary of his understanding, while Israel and Judah love David as he goes before them. These contrasting ruler-and-people responses form the particular parallel; the target does not establish every expectation about military courage or identify the wisdom speaker with David.
triples.source_text: Terrifying rulers will fear me when they hear of me; among the multitude I will appear good, and in war courageous.

target_units.text: Saul was afraid of David.
He removed him from his presence and appointed him a commander of a thousand for himself. He went out and came in before the people.
David showed understanding in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.
Saul saw that he showed great understanding, and he was wary of him.
All Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before the people.

triples.relationship: Fire, smoke and shining eyes in fearsome creature imagery
triples.rationale: Wisdom imagines unknown beasts with fiery breath, smoke and dreadful sparks from their eyes. Job's dragon description gives bright eyes, burning torches and flames from its mouth, and smoke from its nostrils. The shared cluster of fiery bodily images is literary; Wisdom's hypothetical newly created beasts are not identified as an actual Egyptian plague or as Job's single dragon.
triples.source_text: or newly created, unknown beasts full of fury, either breathing a fire-breathing blast, or scattering a stench of smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes,

target_units.text: In its sneeze brightness shines, and its eyes have the appearance of the dawn-bearer.
Burning torches go out from its mouth, and fire-hearths are hurled about.
Smoke comes out of its nostrils, as from a furnace burning with a coal fire.
Its soul is coals, and flame comes out of its mouth.

triples.relationship: Fear attached to a creature's appearance
triples.rationale: Wisdom imagines beasts whose very appearance could terrify and destroy. Job asks who could uncover the creature's face or open its facial gates, with fear surrounding its teeth. Both emphasize the terror of confronting the creature's visible features; Job does not assert Wisdom's further hypothetical destruction by appearance alone.
triples.source_text: whose injury could not only utterly crush them, but whose very appearance could terrify and destroy them.

target_units.text: Who will uncover the face of its clothing, and who could enter the fold of its breastplate?
Who will open the gates of its face? Fear surrounds its teeth.

triples.relationship: Human religious custom treated as binding authority
triples.rationale: Wisdom says an ungodly image-worship custom grew strong and was kept as law. Mark rebukes holding human tradition and establishing it while setting aside God's commandment. Both criticize human religious practice being treated as authoritative; Mark's dispute over inherited observances is not identified with the grieving father's image cult or its historical origin.
triples.source_text: Then, strengthened over time, the ungodly custom was kept as law.

target_units.text: In vain do they worship Me, teaching human commandments as teachings.’
You abandon God’s commandment and hold to human tradition.”
He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!

triples.relationship: Nocturnal sounds and apparitions causing terror
triples.rationale: Wisdom describes terrifying sounds and gloomy specters appearing to those trapped in darkness. Eliphaz recounts nocturnal sound, trembling and a spirit before him, followed by a breeze and voice. Both combine frightening nighttime sounds with an uncanny encounter. Eliphaz explicitly sees no recognizable form, unlike Wisdom's specters with faces, and his episode is not placed in Egypt.
triples.source_text: For not even the recess that held them kept them free from fear; terrifying sounds rang around them, and gloomy specters with unsmiling faces appeared.

target_units.text: There were terrors and a nocturnal sound, fear falling upon people;
a shudder and trembling met me and shook my bones greatly.
A spirit came upon my face, and my hair and flesh shuddered.
I stood up and did not recognize it; I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, but I heard a breeze and a voice:

triples.relationship: Dreams turning hoped-for nighttime rest into fear
triples.rationale: Wisdom's account of a quiet night interrupted by judgment includes dreadful dreams and unexpected fear. Job says that when he expected his bed to comfort him, dreams frightened him and visions overwhelmed him. Both portray disturbing dreams intruding upon nighttime repose; Job is not assigned the firstborn judgment or the guilt of Wisdom's sufferers.
triples.source_text: Then at once apparitions of dreadful dreams disturbed them, and unexpected fears came upon them;

target_units.text: I said, ‘My bed will comfort me; on my couch I will privately bring up a matter with myself,’
Thou frightenest me with dreams and overwhelmest me with visions.

deferred_source_units.source_text: For this man knows better than everyone that he is sinning, when he crafts fragile vessels and carved images from earthy material.
deferred_source_units.reason: Romans 1:21-23 concerns people who knew God but exchanged His glory for images. Wisdom 15:13 gives the craftsman a particular superior awareness that he is sinning, while 15:11 says he did not know his Maker. The different knowledge claims are not flattened into one identical assertion, so this proposed counterpart remains unretained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: For the dreams that troubled them had announced this beforehand, so that they would not perish without knowing why they suffered.
deferred_source_units.reason: Matthew 27:19 reports Pilate's wife suffering in a dream and urging him to avoid the righteous Man. It does not announce the dreamer's own future death or explain why she would die, as Wisdom says its dreams explained impending suffering. The narrower forewarning-and-reason claim remains unsupported by this candidate.
